neighbours.label: word that opens an embedded question or possibility clause (how, whether, chance that) after explain/know/likelihood words
fire: The documentary shows how the bridge was built in just two years.
Doctors are still unsure whether the treatment helps older patients.
There's a strong chance that prices will rise again next month.
The final chapter describes how the villagers rebuilt after the flood.
Investors wondered whether the company could survive another year.
In this lecture she explains how bees communicate through dance.
Tests will reveal whether the water is safe to drink.
There is little chance that the road will reopen before spring.
quiet: The documentary shows the bridge that was built in just two years.
Doctors are still treating older patients with the new drug.
There's a strong smell of smoke in the kitchen again tonight.
The final chapter describes the villagers and their rebuilt homes.
Investors praised the company for surviving another difficult year.
In this lecture she explains the dance that bees use to communicate.
Tests found traces of lead in the water supply.
There is little traffic on the road before spring.

predictions: Fires on how/whether/chance when they introduce a clause as the object of explaining, wondering or likelihood; quiet when the same verbs take a plain noun object.
notes: Card: ' how' x10, ' whether' x9, ' chance' x5 (gate-closed regime). Probes: explains how 0.811, determine whether 0.922, good chance that 0.904, debate whether 0.791; 'explains the railways' 0.042, but 'determine the dose' 0.284 (the verb itself predicts whether) and direct 'asked him how' 0.236. Near misses avoid determine-type verbs.
